curiosity: Why does a soap bubble turn completely pitch black and invisible just a fraction of a second before popping?

titles.desktop: The Secret Physics of Soap Bubbles: Why Thin Films Make Rainbows

desktop_mission.mission_sub: Phase Inversion, Optical Path Interference & Spectral Iridescence
desktop_mission.voice_mission: Today we're simulating thin-film interference and soap bubble iridescence in Kotlin.
math_cards: Reflected waves align in phase with a half-wave shift at the outer surface
Extra optical distance traveled by the refracted beam inside the liquid film
When thickness approaches zero, all visible wavelengths cancel out destructively
desktop_mission.voice_math: The core physics: optical path difference, half-wave phase inversion, and spectral interference intensity.

math_steps.badge: EQUATION 1 OF 3 • OPTICAL PATH & PHASE SHIFT
math_steps.note: Light reflecting off the denser soap film flips phase by 180 degrees
math_steps.sub_desc: Calculates geometric extra distance and reflection phase inversion.

math_steps.formula: I(λ) = I_0 · cos²(Δφ / 2) = I_0 · sin²(π·OPD / λ)
math_steps.note: Each wavelength constructive peak creates distinct iridescent rainbow fringes
math_steps.sub_desc: Computes wavelength-dependent reflectance and interference intensity.

math_steps.badge: EQUATION 3 OF 3 • GRAVITATIONAL DRAINAGE & BLACK FILM
math_steps.formula: d(y) = d_min + k·y  (d < 30 nm -> I ≈ 0, Black Film)
math_steps.note: Gravity thins the top until destructive interference turns the film pitch black

mystery.en: Why does a soap bubble turn completely pitch black right before it pops?

en.title: Soap Bubble Iridescence & Black Films
en.teaser: Light waves reflecting from the outer and inner surfaces superpose to create swirling rainbow bands.

en.hook: Why does a soap bubble display vivid swirling rainbows with zero artificial coloring?
en.math: Light reflecting from the front and back surfaces of the nanometer film interferes, boosting specific colors while canceling others based on thickness.
en.question: Can we simulate thin-film interference and Newton's black film live in Kotlin Multiplatform?
en.code_tip: We calculate optical path differences, evaluate multi-wavelength phase shifts, and render spectral interference fringes on Canvas.
en.payoff: Soap bubble thin-film interference and iridescent fringes running live in Kotlin.
